8	## GDScript (4.5+)
9	
10	- **Variadic arguments**: Functions can accept arbitrary parameter counts. The
11	  rest parameter is written `...name`, comes last, and is typed `Array` or left
12	  untyped — `values: Variant...` and `...values: Array[int]` do not parse
13	  ```gdscript
14	  func log_values(prefix: String, ...values: Array) -> void:
15	      for v in values:
16	          print(prefix, ": ", v)
17	  ```
18	
19	- **Lambdas capture local variables by value** (every Godot 4 version): a local
20	  is captured once, when the lambda is created, and a lambda cannot reassign an
21	  outer local — `var hit := false` / `func(): hit = true` leaves the caller's
22	  `hit` false. Share state through a reference type (a Dictionary, an Array or
23	  an object) and mutate its contents. A rest parameter works in a lambda too, so
24	  `func(...args)` connects to a signal with any number of arguments (observed on
25	  4.6.1; a one-argument lambda on a zero-argument signal errors "Method expected
26	  1 argument(s), but called with 0")
27	  ```gdscript
28	  var state := {"emitted": false}
29	  some_signal.connect(func(...args): state.emitted = true)
30	  ```
31	
32	- **Abstract classes and methods**: Use `@abstract` to enforce inheritance
33	  ```gdscript
34	  @abstract
35	  class_name BaseEnemy extends CharacterBody3D
36	
37	  # No body: "a newline or a semicolon is expected after the function header".
38	  # Subclasses MUST override it.
39	  @abstract func get_attack_pattern() -> Array[Attack]
40	  ```
41	
42	- **Script backtracing**: Detailed call stacks available even in Release builds

45	
46	- **An override of a typed method inherits its return type**, so it needs an
47	  explicit `return` statement; the migration guide's fix is `return null`
48	- **Writing one element of a packed array no longer calls the property's
49	  setter.** A setter on a `PackedInt32Array` (etc.) property no longer runs on
50	  `arr[i] = v`; assign the whole array where the setter has to run

137	### 3. The block, the hook and what the kernel is told (ADR-BODY-02, ADR-0003 § 2)
138	
139	**Registration** (all fields mandatory, ADR-0003 § 2; the GDD's BDY-5 list is completed with the three fields it predates):
140	
141	| Field | Value |
142	|---|---|
143	| `block_id` / `owner_name` | `&"body.state"` / `&"body"` |
144	| `schema_version` / `supported_versions` | 1 / `[1]` |
145	| `block_class` | `SIM` (never `PERCEPTION_OUT`; no per-player variant, TR-shipbody-029) |
146	| `persist` / `persist_scope` / `scope` | true / `WORLD` / `SHARED` |
147	| `gameplay` | **true** (hooks and Assembly/Transit applies change it; the paused-write test applies) |
148	| `interpolated` | **true** (§ 8): the previous/current pair is Body's derived `pos_prev` and `world_prev`; `commit_baseline` and `snap_baseline` are therefore mandatory and supplied |
149	| `repl_hint` | `SHARED_SUMMARY` (unused until VS-B) |
150	| `restore_after` | `[&"layout.state"]` |
151	| callables | `snapshot`, `restore`, `default_state`, `post_restore`, `read_view`, `empty_view`, `commit_baseline`, `snap_baseline`, `binding_source` (the seat binding source of BDY-7); no `init_world` (Web Map's `init_world` calls BM1 and BM7 inside the `INIT` scope) |
152	| commands | **none**. Body registers no `CommandTypeDescriptor` and subscribes to no Layout dirty key (BDY-21) |
153	| hook | `HookDescriptor{hook_id &"body.integrate", owner_name &"body", divisor 1, offset 0, after [{id &"controller.step", tolerates_stale false}, {id &"layout.doors", tolerates_stale false}], callable}` |
154	| key space | `KeySpaceDescriptor` kinds `[2, 4]` named `[BODY, ACT]`; event ids `[1, 2, 3]` named `[BODY_TRANSFER, BODY_DOCK_CONTACT, BODY_HULL_SEPARATION]`; `quiet_writes_allowed = false` |
155	| fault domain | `register_fault_domain(BodyFaults.DOMAIN_ID /* 5 */, &"body", BodyFaults.NAMES)` |
156	| diagnostics | one channel `body.diag` (field list is ADR-0031's) |
157	| PROJECTOR subscriber | **not registered here**: `body.projector` is ADR-0034's class and subscribes to `body.state` through the facets of ADR-0004 and ADR-0009 |
158	
159	**Hook order.** `body.integrate` is a **partial order**: after `controller.step` and `layout.doors`, which are mutually unordered. `controller.step` follows `suit.vitals` (ADR-0019 § 2.4); `emitter.place` is `after: [body.integrate, graph.propagate.failure]` (ADR-0017); `controller.noise` is `after: [{id: body.integrate, tolerates_stale: false}]` (ADR-0019 § 2.4) and `horror.step` is after `body.integrate` (ADR-0023, § 12 fixture). All four are divisor 1, so the `STALE_EDGE_UNDECLARED` boot warning cannot fire for them. An unknown hook id fails boot (`UNKNOWN_DEPENDENCY`), so the ids Body names are exactly the ones their owners register: `controller.step`, `layout.doors`, `suit.vitals`, `emitter.place`, `controller.noise`, `horror.step`.
160	
161	**Why `gameplay = true` and not a derived block.** Body's persisted state changes during play, so it is not `persist = false`, and a paused kernel must not let a `PAUSED_APPLY` write it (ADR-0003 § 4: `PAUSED_APPLY` opens only blocks named in a command's `writes_blocks`; no pausable command names `body.state`).
162	
163	**Why one block and not two.** A `body.frames` block next to `body.state` would add a second restore node, a second owner registration and a split between a pose row and the actors standing on it that a weld's single apply must keep consistent. The GDD rejected it (BDY-5); this ADR agrees: the two tables share `restore`, `snapshot`, one hash and one dirty-key space.
164	
165	### 4. State shape: id-sorted struct-of-arrays (ADR-BODY-02, TR-shipbody-003, -006, -014)
166	
167	#### 4.1 Persisted columns (`BodyState`)
168	
169	```gdscript
170	class_name BodyState extends RefCounted
171	# scalar
172	var next_actor_id: int = 1                   # allocated here, never reused (CR-8); first id 1
173	# actors: parallel columns, ascending actor_id, row = bsearch position (never cached across a mutator)
174	var a_id: PackedInt64Array        # int64 (a 2^53+7 id must not truncate)
175	var a_kind: PackedInt32Array      # BodyIds.KIND_SEAT = 1, KIND_AGENT = 2 (0 is invalid); append-only
176	var a_seat: PackedInt32Array      # PlayerId >= 1 for SEAT; 0 for AGENT
177	var a_body: PackedInt32Array      # Layout body_id (< 2^31)
178	var a_x: PackedInt32Array         # pos_curr, body-frame base px (may be negative after a detach re-base)
179	var a_y: PackedInt32Array
180	var a_sub_x: PackedInt32Array     # residue, 1/256 px, |sub| <= 255
181	var a_sub_y: PackedInt32Array
182	var a_oct: PackedInt32Array       # last_octant 0..7, 8 = NONE: Body's own record, not the Controller's
183	var a_odo: PackedInt64Array       # int64 odometer, travels as a native int64 in the binary payload
184	# bodies: SPARSE (a missing row means world 0, vel 0, heading 0), ascending body_id
185	var b_id: PackedInt32Array
186	var b_wx: PackedInt32Array        # world pose of the body-frame origin, whole base px, |.| <= WORLD_COORD_LIMIT
187	var b_wy: PackedInt32Array
188	var b_vx: PackedInt32Array        # whole base px per tick, |.| <= VEL_MAX_PX_PER_TICK
189	var b_vy: PackedInt32Array
190	var b_head: PackedInt32Array      # heading_q: reserved, MUST be 0, persisted so a future rotation is a schema bump
191	```
192	
193	`kind` values are assigned here (the GDD names the two kinds and fixes no number): `SEAT = 1`, `AGENT = 2`, append-only. Int32 is sufficient for every position column because a body-frame coordinate is bounded by section extents (tens of thousands of px) and a world coordinate by `WORLD_COORD_LIMIT` (2^22 in TR-shipbody-026). Only `a_id` and `a_odo` are int64, exactly the GDD's two s64 columns (AC-BDY-137: an odometer of 2^53 + 7 must not truncate).
194	
195	**Sparse form is canonical.** A body row whose six values are `(world 0, 0), (vel 0, 0), heading 0` is **deleted**, never stored (BM6, BM7 delete it); `restore` rejects such a row as `BDY_RESTORE_NONCANONICAL`, otherwise `snapshot(restore(x)) != x`. `MAX_BODIES` (Layout's) bounds the table.
196	
197	#### 4.2 Derived columns (`BodyDerived`), never persisted, never hashed, never replicated
198	
199	```gdscript
200	class_name BodyDerived extends RefCounted
201	var a_px: PackedInt32Array        # pos_prev x   (index-aligned with BodyState.a_*)
202	var a_py: PackedInt32Array
203	var a_blocked: PackedByteArray    # 1 = a non-zero step was requested and nothing moved
204	var b_wpx: PackedInt32Array       # world_prev (index-aligned with BodyState.b_*)
205	var b_wpy: PackedInt32Array
206	var loco_state: LocoState         # caller-owned scratch, allocated once at setup
207	var loco_intent: LocoIntent
208	var loco_result: LocoResult
209	var buffer: QueryBuffer           # ADR-0014's buffer type, sized at setup to MAX_FOOTPRINT_RECTS_PER_BODY
210	var counters: PackedInt64Array    # indexed by BodyIds.CNT_*; reset by tests only
211	```
212	
213	Two private functions, `_actor_row_insert(idx)` and `_actor_row_remove(idx)` (and the body pair), are the **only** code that touches both column sets, so the persisted and derived columns cannot drift; a unit test asserts equal lengths after every mutator, every restore and every hook run. A reflection test classifies every member of `BodyState` and `BodyDerived` as persisted or derived (the ADR-0011 pattern) and a zero-and-diff test zeroes every derived member and checks `snapshot()` bytes unchanged.
214	
215	**Row index discipline.** A row index is found by `bsearch` at the start of a call and is valid only until the next write to that table. No row index, `Dictionary` key, section id or `actor_section` answer is cached across a mutator or a restore (TR-shipbody-028; a stale section id is the failure mode).
216	
217	#### 4.3 Why struct-of-arrays now, and what would reverse it
218	
219	The GDD treated SoA as a working assumption and opened Open Question 46 (SoA versus array-of-records). **Decision: SoA.** Eight actors and eight bodies are tiny; what matters is that the hook visits every actor every tick and a `RefCounted` per actor would add an object dereference per field read, and that a typed `Array[ActorRow]` makes the snapshot a per-row copy while columns copy as ten and six `duplicate()` calls. The snapshot shape (§ 5) is independent of the in-memory layout, so **spike S1 can reverse this with no schema change** (V6). Insertion is by `bsearch` plus `insert` and removal is `remove_at`, kept sorted by the mutators and never sorted at tick time (V1 probed both on `PackedInt64Array`). Iterating a `Dictionary` is never used for any table (insertion order after erase and re-insert is not a hashing input).
220	
221	#### 4.4 Ids and the dirty-key width
222	
223	`actor_id` is int64 but a dirty key's `id` must fit 32 bits (ADR-0004 § 3: `DirtyKey.make(kind, id)`, `id <= 0xFFFFFFFF`). Ids are never reused, so a very long campaign could in principle grow the counter, but at the MVP (one actor per seat, respawn rows, `MAX_ACTORS` live) 2^32 is unreachable. It is nevertheless stated: `can_place` refuses with `BDY_PLACE_ID_EXHAUSTED` when `next_actor_id > ACTOR_ID_KEY_MAX` (0xFFFFFFFF), and `restore` rejects an `actor_id` or `next_actor_id` above it as `BDY_RESTORE_ACTOR_ID`. Body ids are Layout's (31-bit), so they always fit.
224	
225	### 5. Collision: one query, one analytic clamp, the stepper as oracle (ADR-BODY-01, TR-shipbody-017, -018, -019, -036)
226	
227	#### 5.1 The seam to Layout: `CollideSource`
228	
229	```gdscript
230	@abstract
231	class_name CollideSource extends RefCounted
232	# Binds the body frame this source answers for (called once per actor-tick, before query_into).
233	@abstract func bind(body_id: int) -> void
234	# Fills `out` with the SOLID rectangles of the bound body that intersect the half-open box
235	# [ax0, ax1) x [ay0, ay1), body-frame base px, unique, ascending rect_key; returns the count.
236	# Allocation-free. Zero-length rectangles are omitted by Layout.
237	@abstract func query_into(ax0: int, ay0: int, ax1: int, ay1: int, out: QueryBuffer) -> int
238	# true iff the foot ORIGIN (x, y) lies in a section of the bound body (Layout section_at != NONE).
239	@abstract func origin_in_body(x: int, y: int) -> bool
240	```
241	
242	The production implementation `LayoutCollide` (in `src/sim/body/`, `extends CollideSource`) wraps ADR-0014's `solid_in_into(body_id, ax0, ay0, ax1, ay1, out)` and ADR-0013's `section_at`. Horror (ADR-0023) supplies its own implementation bound to its body; tests supply a rectangle-list double. **Assumption on ADR-0014 (forward reference, § Related):** `QueryBuffer` exposes at least `x0`, `y0`, `x1`, `y1` as `PackedInt32Array` (body frame, half-open), `keys` as `PackedInt64Array` and a `count`, sized once at boot to `MAX_FOOTPRINT_RECTS_PER_BODY`; the result is the SOLID set in its **current leaf state** for the tick (post-cut from P2, post-`layout.doors` from P3); there is no inflated margin, no "perceived" variant and no second rectangle set. If ADR-0014 names the columns differently, `LayoutCollide` absorbs the difference and nothing else changes.
243	
244	**Why an `@abstract` port and not a `Callable`.** The GDD binds `collide` to `solid_in_into` "once at boot". A stored `Callable` invoked with `.call(` is a `SIM-12` dynamic-dispatch finding and `Callable(` / `.bind(` are `HOT-01` tokens; an abstract-class method call is a direct typed call, mockable and lint-clean. The cost is one method call per query, not per rectangle (V5 measures it).
245	
246	**Unordered input is tolerated.** The sweep takes a minimum over candidates, so duplicates, an empty result and any order give the identical `moved`; in debug builds `query_into` results are checked for strictly ascending `keys` and a violation increments `diag.solid_in_unordered` (TR-shipbody-036; the order guarantee is ADR-0014's, the tolerance is Body's).
247	
248	#### 5.2 The query box (D.12)
249	
250	For an actor at `pos` with requested whole-pixel steps `(sx, sy)`, `|sx|, |sy| <= 3`, the single query is the Minkowski cover of the foot box over the x-then-y path:
251	`[pos.x - hw + mini(0, sx), pos.x + hw + maxi(0, sx)) x [pos.y + mini(0, sy), pos.y + FH + maxi(0, sy))` with `hw = FOOT_BOX_W >> 1` and `FH = FOOT_BOX_H` (at most 19 by 11 cells). The y-phase foot box lies inside this cover because the x-phase moved at most `|sx|` pixels toward the cover's edge. A rectangle the query does not return cannot be hit by construction. **A stationary actor** (move octant NONE, or both steps zero after the residue update) **issues no query**.
252	
253	#### 5.3 The analytic clamp (non-exempt actor)
254	
255	Let `E` be the set of returned rectangles whose half-open intersection with the **start** foot box is non-empty (cell count `ov(r) > 0`); `E` is computed from the query result at the start of the actor's tick and fixed for that tick. 257	- **x axis.** Consider each returned rectangle `r` whose y-range overlaps the box's (`r.y0 < by1 and r.y1 > by0`). 258	- **y axis**, run after the x axis with the box at its post-x position: the same with the roles swapped (rectangles whose x-range overlaps the box's; south limit `r.y0 - by1`, north limit `by0 - r.y1`).

260	This is exactly what the 1-px loop returns: a rectangle blocks at the first pixel at which the destination box intersects it, every later pixel is also blocked (moving further toward it cannot clear it), and the loop's first refusal stops the axis. 262	**First-legal-row corollary (the designed examples).** Walking north into a wall whose footprint rows are `[y0, y0 + 24)`, the box rests with `pos.y = y0 + 24`; walking south it rests with `pos.y = y0 - FOOT_BOX_H` (box bottom flush). Walking into a wall adds 0 to the odometer.

271	
272	The literal 1-px stepper (`SweepOracle`) is the specification: before each pixel the destination box is tested against every candidate (non-`E` fully solid; `E` by condition (a); containment (b) when `E` is non-empty); the first refusal stops that axis. 273	
274	**Decision:** the analytic clamp is the **shipped baseline**; the stepper is the oracle and a debug cross-check mode (`BODY_SWEEP_CHECK`, off in release, compares both for every actor-tick in a CI soak and fails on any difference).

396	|---|---|---|
397	| 1 to 15 | `BDY_RESTORE_VERSION`, `_TYPE`, `_COUNT`, `_ACTOR_ID`, `_KIND`, `_OCTANT`, `_SUB_RANGE`, `_SUB_INVARIANT`, `_ODOMETER`, `_HEADING_UNSUPPORTED`, `_POSE_RANGE`, `_CAPACITY`, `_ORDER`, `_NONCANONICAL`, `_UNKNOWN_BODY` | `restore` via `ctx.fault` (§ 11) |
398	| 16 to 21 | `BDY_PLACE_UNKNOWN_BODY`, `_PLACE_INSIDE_FOOTPRINT`, `_PLACE_CAPACITY`, `_PLACE_BAD_KIND`, `_PLACE_DUPLICATE_SEAT`, `_PLACE_ID_EXHAUSTED` | BM1 apply-time re-check; BM5 uses the first two |
399	| 22 | `BDY_UNKNOWN_ACTOR` | BM2, BM5 |
400	| 23 to 27 | `BDY_REBASE_SAME_BODY`, `_REBASE_UNKNOWN_BODY`, `_REBASE_SECTION_NOT_OWNED`, `_REBASE_SHIFT_OFF_GRID`, `_REBASE_ACTOR_IN_CAP` | BM3, BM4 |
401	| 28, 29 | `BDY_VEL_UNKNOWN_BODY`, `BDY_VEL_OUT_OF_RANGE` | BM6, also a `can_rebase_detach` reason |

404	
405	(Local 21 `BDY_PLACE_ID_EXHAUSTED` and local 32 are the two additions to the GDD's reason set.)
406	
407	**Check-then-write, fail-closed (TR-shipbody-020, -040).** Each mutator evaluates its **whole** apply-time predicate before its first write. On a defect it (a) writes nothing (tables, `next_actor_id`, dirty set, event queue exactly as before), (b) calls `sink.report(mutator_id, code)` (default sink: increments `BDY_PLAN_MISMATCH`, active in every build; in debug it also `push_error`s), (c) calls `scope.fault(code, detail)` so the scope closes and the caller's later mutators write nothing (ADR-0003 § 5), and (d) returns `-code`. The caller, per ADR-0003, returns `ctx.complete()` at once after the first negative status. No path uses `assert()` (compiled out of release; `SIM-11`). The GDD's injectable `plan_mismatch_sink` Callable becomes the `@abstract` port `PlanMismatchSink` (`report(mutator_id: int, code: int) -> void`) with `CountingSink` (default) and `RecordingSink` (tests), because `Callable.call(` is a `SIM-12` token; tests exercise every defect in the ordinary debug gdUnit4 runner.
408	
409	**The one saturate-and-continue branch must not fault.** BM4's new pose row, when `world_old + shift` leaves `±WORLD_COORD_LIMIT` or `vel_old` plus drift leaves `±VEL_MAX_PX_PER_TICK`, **saturates and returns `OK`**: the sink counts `BDY_WORLD_LIMIT` (where applicable) and `BDY_PLAN_MISMATCH`, and **`scope.fault` is not called**, because the Graph and Layout have already applied the cut and a fault would kill the rest of the apply. A row `restore` would reject (`BDY_RESTORE_POSE_RANGE`) would make the next autosave unloadable, so this branch is load-bearing (the death-restart policy restores the last autosave). Class (i) defects are checked first: a call with both an unknown new body and a range overflow returns the code.
410	
411	**BM1 `place_actor`.** Allocates `actor_id` from `next_actor_id` (first id 1, never reused after removal), inserts the row at its `bsearch` position with `pos_prev := pos_curr`, `sub := (0, 0)`, `last_octant := NONE`, `odometer := 0`, runs the BDY-16 detection event for the new actor (a placement inside a SOLID rectangle is refused: `BDY_PLACE_INSIDE_FOOTPRINT`). Preconditions (`can_place`): body live in Layout (`BodyLayoutPort.body_is_live`), foot box clear of every SOLID rectangle (one `query_into`), `actor_count < MAX_ACTORS`, `kind` is `SEAT` or `AGENT`, a `SEAT` has `seat >= 1` and an `AGENT` has `seat == 0`, no other `SEAT` row has this seat, `next_actor_id <= ACTOR_ID_KEY_MAX`. Marks `ACT/<id>`.
412	
413	**BM2 `remove_actor`.** Deletes the row (and the derived row); marks `ACT/<id>`.
414	
415	**BM3 `rebase_on_attach(surviving, absorbed, shift_x, shift_y)` (weld).** Only actors on the **absorbed** body are touched: `pos_curr += shift`, `body_id := surviving`, `pos_prev := pos_curr`, `sub` and `last_octant` kept (a whole-pixel shift cannot disturb a residue). Host-body actors are untouched ("a weld moves nothing already built"). The absorbed pose row is deleted (its `vel` is discarded; the survivor's row is unchanged). Emits one `BODY_TRANSFER` per moved actor (`frame_delta = +shift`) and one `BODY_DOCK_CONTACT`. Checks: the two ids differ (`BDY_REBASE_SAME_BODY`), both live in Layout (`BDY_REBASE_UNKNOWN_BODY`), `shift` on Layout's 24-px grid (`BDY_REBASE_SHIFT_OFF_GRID`, a Layout defect). The mutator runs in P2 and `body.integrate` in P3 of the same tick, so the shifted actor is stepped this tick from the shifted position with a zero interpolation delta. **Invariant (a test, TR-shipbody-023):** for every moved actor `(actor_section, actor_local_px)` is identical before and after, and `abs = world(body) + pos_curr` is conserved iff the docking invariant holds (§ 10).
416	
417	**BM4 `rebase_on_detach(old, new, moved_sections, shift_x, shift_y, cap_rects)` (cut).** Order: (1) the **whole predicate first**: ids differ and live, every `moved_sections` member is owned by `new` (`BDY_REBASE_SECTION_NOT_OWNED`: the call-order trap, because Layout's mutator has already run), `shift` on the grid, and `actors_overlapping(old, cap_rects)` is empty (`-BDY_REBASE_ACTOR_IN_CAP` otherwise, writing nothing; Body rules REFUSE, never EJECT: the 2026-10-28 delegated ruling G6). (2) For each actor on `old`, in ascending `actor_id`, the **side is the section containing its foot ORIGIN evaluated against the reconstructed pre-cut geometry**: for `s` in `moved_sections`, the pre-cut offset is `section_offset(s) + shift` (Layout has already re-based them); the origin is in `s` iff `BodyLayoutPort.section_contains(s, x - (offset_x(s) + shift_x), y - (offset_y(s) + shift_y))` (containment is by the section's floor area, never a bounding box, because hull-abutting sections have overlapping bounding boxes); an origin in no moved section is tested against the remaining body with the unchanged `section_at(old, x, y)`; an origin in no section at all stays on `old` and counts `BDY_TRANSFER_NO_SECTION` (defect-only; CI asserts zero in a clean build). (3) Actors on the new side: `pos_curr -= shift`, `body_id := new`, `pos_prev := pos_curr`, `sub := (0, 0)`, `last_octant` kept (harmless, `sub` is zero); one `BODY_TRANSFER` each (`frame_delta = -shift`). (4) Creates the new pose row: `world := world_old + shift`, `vel := vel_old` plus the default-zero drift, so both halves co-move; `world_prev := world`. (5) Emits `BODY_HULL_SEPARATION`. (6) Runs the BDY-16 detection event for every actor on the touched bodies (moved or not), because the SOLID set changed under them. **A cut cannot create the cap trap**, because step (1) refuses it. **Conservation (TR-shipbody-024, -048):** detach conserves `abs` exactly for every actor on either side. **A weld followed by a cut of the same seam is not in general the identity on `pos_curr`** (detach re-bases to the minimum section id of the new component, ADR-0013 § 7; a weld shifts by the absorbed offset), so any round-trip test asserts `abs` and `(section, section-local)`, never raw `pos_curr`.
418	
419	**BM5 `transfer_actor(actor_id, to_body_id, x, y, cause)` (pod hop).** `pos_curr := (x, y)`, `body_id := to_body_id`, `pos_prev := pos_curr`, `sub := (0, 0)`, `last_octant` kept; emits `BODY_TRANSFER{pod}` with `frame_delta = (x, y) - pos_curr(old)`. Body never searches for a free arrival cell (that would be a displacement): `can_transfer` answers `BDY_PLACE_INSIDE_FOOTPRINT` and Transit owns the alternative; two crewmates arriving at one cell is legal. `cause` is `POD` at the MVP.
420	
421	**BM3, BM4, BM5 change only `body_id`, `pos_curr`, `pos_prev` and `sub` of an actor row** and nothing in `controller.state` (carry, DEAD state, channel fields). The Controller holds no write on Body and clears only its own channel fields on a body edge (ADR-0019 § 1.3), so a same-tick Controller write after a pod hop cannot displace the arrival cell (TR-shipbody-048; the property test runs a hop and a Controller tick in one scope and compares `controller.state` bytes).
422	
423	**BM6 `set_body_velocity`** creates or updates the pose row's `vel` (a zero velocity on a zero-world row deletes it); **BM7 `set_body_pose`** creates or updates `world_x, world_y` and leaves `vel`; it raises no event and touches no actor row, so the interior is unchanged (BDY-2). `can_set_pose` rejects `abs(coord) > WORLD_COORD_LIMIT` (`BDY_POSE_OUT_OF_RANGE`). BM7's only caller is Web Map & Transit inside the atomic applies the Web Map GDD lists (`init_world`, departure, `pod_arrive`, `pod_settle`, `berth`, `unberth`, each `berth_step`); a re-origin is a pure translation of every live body in one apply (ADR-0026's lint `REORIGIN_IS_TRANSLATION`), so no `rebase_world` mutator exists, and a dormant body's pose is never read by the simulation (lint `BDY-04`, § 12) (TR-webmap-008).
424	
425	**Consistency after every call, including every call that returned a code or saturated (TR-shipbody-040).** Five invariants hold: I1 every `actor_id` is unique, ascending and below `next_actor_id`; I2 body rows ascend and none is canonical-empty; I3 every `body_id` in either table is live in Layout; I4 `restore(snapshot())` accepts the block; I5 the derived columns are index-aligned with the persisted ones. A property test runs a generated mutator sequence (valid and defective calls, including each fault path and the saturating BM4) and checks I1 to I5 after **every** call.
426	
427	**Weld legality takes no pose input (TR-shipbody-025).** It is Layout's `can_attach` plus the Graph's `can_join` and nothing else. `docked(a, b, shift_x, shift_y) -> bool` is a pure read (equal `vel` on both bodies and `world_b - world_a == shift`, which lies on the 24-px grid by Layout D.6) offered to Assembly and Transit and **gating nothing inside Body**. A PLAYER-origin weld is OFFERED only when `docked` holds; this is a named must-repeat for ADR-0021 and ADR-0026 (the offer gate is the only guard of the exterior hull jump; the camera cut hides camera motion, not the absorbed hull's jump).
428	
429	### 10. Pose, velocity and the inertial interior (BDY-2, BDY-26 to BDY-28; TR-shipbody-004, -026)
430	
431	**World pose is exterior-only.** `world_*` locates the body-frame origin in the exterior frame; `vel_*` is whole base px per tick (no sub-pixel exterior residue in schema v1; a slower drift would be a schema bump). `body.integrate` adds `vel` to `world` once per tick, before any actor steps (§ 7). **Nothing keyed on a body-frame coordinate reads `world_*` or `vel_*`.** The proof is a fixture: set a non-zero `vel` on the avatar's body, run 600 ticks, and compare `canonical_encode(snapshot()["actors"])` with a body at rest: byte-identical (TR-shipbody-004). A lint (`BDY-04`) backs it: the getters `world_x`, `world_y`, `vel_x`, `vel_y`, `world_prev_*` and `world_pose` may be named only in `src/sim/web/`, `src/sim/assembly/` (for `docked`), `src/presentation/` and Body itself.
432	
433	**The interior is an inertial frame.** Ship motion applies no force, push, tilt, drift or knockback to any actor; nothing moves an actor except `LocomotionStep` and the transfer arithmetic of BM3, BM4, BM5. `DETACH_DRIFT_PX_PER_TICK` is locked at 0 until the Vertical Slice defines an axis and a sign (schema range `[0, 0]`, boot error otherwise; the interior never sees it).
434	
435	**Range and the float32 bound.** `|world| <= WORLD_COORD_LIMIT` (2^22) and `|vel| <= VEL_MAX_PX_PER_TICK` (16 per tick); `heading_q` must be 0 and is rejected on restore (`BDY_RESTORE_HEADING_UNSUPPORTED`, the mirror of Layout's `rot_q`). The 2^22 bound exists so that a canvas offset, the difference of two world coordinates and therefore within ±2^23, stays inside the range `Node2D.position` represents exactly (V3, probed 2026-10-29: `2^23 + 1` round-trips, `2^24 + 1` collapses to `2^24`). This closes BDY-26's `[UNV: build precision]` for the **standard editor build**; the release-export repeat and the camera math are ADR-0008's. If a release probe fails, the fallback is TR-shipbody-038's: a sign-split expression or a lower `WORLD_COORD_LIMIT`, which is a schema bump by the bounds ledger of § 2. Web Map & Transit's own budget (`WEB_COORD_BUDGET_PX` at most `WORLD_COORD_LIMIT / 32`) is stated against the default and is a Web Map lint.
436	
437	**Derived exterior interpolation state.** `world_prev` (§ 8) is reset to the new `world` on every discontinuous write (BM7, BM4's new row, BM6 deleting a row, the `BDY_WORLD_LIMIT` freeze, `post_restore`, `snap_baseline`). The renderer computes `canvas_offset_render(b, tick_alpha) = floor(off_prev + (off_curr - off_prev) * tick_alpha)` per axis with `off_curr = world(b) - world(avatar_body)` and `off_prev = world_prev(b) - world_prev(avatar_body)` (the **current** avatar body for both, so a body switch never interpolates across two reference frames). That formula is a presentation computation (ADR-0008, ADR-0034); Body only publishes `world`, `world_prev` and `vel`.
438	
439	### 11. Persistence, restore idempotence, the read view and events (ADR-BODY-02, TR-shipbody-006, -008, -009, -028, -029, -040, -041, -043)
440	
441	#### 11.1 The snapshot payload: five keys, plain Arrays
442	
443	`snapshot(ctx)` puts a plain `Dictionary` with **exactly five keys** (TR-shipbody-008; the shape is independent of the in-memory columns):
444	
445	| Key | Type | Content |
446	|---|---|---|
447	| `next_actor_id` | int | the counter |
448	| `n_bodies` | int | pose rows |
449	| `n_actors` | int | actor rows |
450	| `bodies` | `Array` of ints, `n_bodies * 6` | row-major, ascending `body_id`: `body_id, world_x, world_y, vel_x, vel_y, heading_q` |
451	| `actors` | `Array` of ints, `n_actors * 10` | row-major, ascending `actor_id`: `actor_id, kind, seat, body_id, pos_x, pos_y, sub_x, sub_y, last_octant, odometer` |
452	
453	No float, no `pos_prev`, no `blocked`, no diagnostic, no `Vector2i`, and `odometer` is never placed in a `Vector2i`. The int64 columns are copied into plain `Array`s at snapshot time (native int64 elements, exact for 2^53 + 7), ids are already ascending (the mutators keep the tables sorted; `snapshot()` verifies sortedness in debug and sorts only a table a defective caller left unsorted, never taking `Dictionary` order), and the arrays are fresh builds (never a live reference to a column, ADR-0003 § 2). **The canonical bytes are the kernel's, not Body's**: the TLV encoding of exactly this payload (`CanonicalEncoder`, ADR-0005: DICT keys sorted by `String(key)` code point, i.e. `actors, bodies, n_actors, n_bodies, next_actor_id`; every int an 8-byte little-endian INT), so s32 and s64 widths no longer exist in the bytes. Body ships no byte writer and never uses `var_to_bytes` for any hashed byte (`DET-01`; TR-shipbody-008).
454	
455	**Why plain Arrays when ADR-0006 permits Packed arrays.** ADR-0006 allows `PackedInt32Array` and `PackedInt64Array` in a payload and ADR-0011 and ADR-0013 use them for their large tables. Body's payload is at most `MAX_ACTORS * 10 + MAX_BODIES * 6 + 3` integers (a few hundred bytes), so the Array-of-int cost is negligible, and TR-shipbody-008 fixes "plain Arrays". The practical advantage is in restore: a decoded payload is a `Variant` tree in which a float, a string or a bool can sit in a slot (a hand-edited or corrupt save, a JSON dump-save), and the type walk of `BDY_RESTORE_TYPE` is exactly what keeps a float from being silently truncated into a range-valid integer and breaking `snapshot(restore(x)) == x`. A packed array would hide that class by construction on the binary path and would still need the walk on the JSON path. The `Array` form costs one pass over ~200 elements at restore (cold path) and is the form the golden file (AC-BDY-110) hashes.
456	
457	#### 11.2 `restore(data, stored_version, ctx)`: two-phase, first failure wins, never clamps
458	
459	Phase 1 decodes and validates into a scratch (cold path, allocation allowed) and on the **first** failure calls `ctx.fault(BodyFaults.<CODE>, detail)` and writes nothing, leaving the live block untouched; phase 2, only on success, copies the contents into the existing `BodyState` columns (each column assigned from the scratch's own arrays, none aliasing `data`; **the object is never replaced**, because the read facade is long-lived, ADR-0003 § 2) and rebuilds `BodyDerived`. Reporting is **only** through `ctx.fault`, never a return tuple, and the callable ends `return ctx.complete()`. Validation order:
460	
461	1. `stored_version` in `[1]` and the key set is exactly the five keys: `BDY_RESTORE_VERSION`.
462	2. Every element of `bodies` and `actors` is a plain integer (not a float, bool, string, null; no missing field): `BDY_RESTORE_TYPE` (this runs before every range check).
463	3. `n_bodies`, `n_actors` non-negative and column lengths exactly `n_bodies * 6` and `n_actors * 10`: `BDY_RESTORE_COUNT`.
464	4. Per row, in row order: `actor_id` at least 1, below `next_actor_id` and at most `ACTOR_ID_KEY_MAX` (`BDY_RESTORE_ACTOR_ID`; a duplicate id is also this code); `kind` is `SEAT` or `AGENT`, `seat` is non-negative, an `AGENT` has seat 0, a `SEAT` has seat at least 1 and no two `SEAT` rows share a seat (`BDY_RESTORE_KIND`); `last_octant` in 0..8 (`BDY_RESTORE_OCTANT`); `abs(sub)` at most 255 (`BDY_RESTORE_SUB_RANGE`); the residue invariant: a non-zero `sub` with `last_octant` NONE, a sign opposing `UNIT[last_octant]`, a non-zero off-axis residue for a cardinal octant, or `abs(sub_x) != abs(sub_y)` on a diagonal octant (`BDY_RESTORE_SUB_INVARIANT`); `odometer` non-negative (`BDY_RESTORE_ODOMETER`); `heading_q == 0` (`BDY_RESTORE_HEADING_UNSUPPORTED`); `abs(world)` and `abs(vel)` within the **current** limits (`BDY_RESTORE_POSE_RANGE`); actor count at most `MAX_ACTORS` (`BDY_RESTORE_CAPACITY`).
465	5. Body rows strictly ascending by `body_id` (a duplicate is `BDY_RESTORE_ORDER`), actor rows ascending by `actor_id` (`BDY_RESTORE_ORDER`), and no body row with world and vel both `(0, 0)` (`BDY_RESTORE_NONCANONICAL`).

466	6. Every `body_id` in either table is live in Layout, checked against the already-restored `layout.state` through `BodyLayoutPort` (`restore_after: [layout.state]` guarantees it restored first): `BDY_RESTORE_UNKNOWN_BODY`.
467	
468	A foot box found overlapping a SOLID rectangle after restore is **not** a failure (a template that changed between builds must not make a save unloadable): BDY-16 applies and the counter runs.
469	
470	**Why a restore is idempotent and `body.state` is not in `REBASE_BLOCKS` (TR-shipbody-041).** `REBASE_BLOCKS` is the closed list of ADR-0006 § 2.2 / SL-12 of blocks for which `snapshot(restore(snapshot()))` may differ from the stored bytes. For `body.state`: (a) `restore` accepts only canonical rows and never clamps, so every accepted payload re-encodes to itself; (b) the sparse rule (`NONCANONICAL`) removes the one place two payloads could mean the same state; (c) no derived value enters the payload; (d) `post_restore` reads and writes only derived columns. Therefore the round trip is byte-identical for `body.state` alone, the membership question has a fixed answer (**not a member**), and the test is the GDD's: restore and re-snapshot at every tick of a 600-tick run in three phases (cardinal, diagonal with `sub != 0`, stopped), plus a synthetic odometer of 2^53 + 7. This is a per-block idempotence fact; ADR-0006 § 2.2 fixes only the mechanism (§ Related lists the one-line ask).
471	
472	**`post_restore(ctx)`** (a) derives `pos_prev := pos_curr`, `world_prev := world`; (b) re-checks Layout liveness as a **diagnostic** only (once every block has restored the kernel holds no intact prior state to fall back to); (c) runs the trapped-actor probe (§ 11.4) for every exempt actor, diagnostic only. **A restore never rebuilds the kernel's seat binding itself**: the kernel's `LOADING` pass does, from Body's `binding_source` callable, which puts `PackedInt64Array` pairs `[seat, actor_id, seat, actor_id, ...]` in ascending `seat` (`SEAT` rows only, derived from the table on each call, no persisted field) via `ctx.put` (the payload shape is not fixed by ADR-0002 § 4 and is an ask). `seat` is persisted precisely because the binding table is not saved. `snap_baseline` then runs on entry to `RUNNING`.
473	
474	**`default_state(ctx)`** puts the empty block (`next_actor_id` 1, no rows). A key held across a restore reads `N` versus `N` in Body's own `last_octant` comparison and the residue continues; a key released during the save/load window resets `sub` exactly as a stop does in uninterrupted play. The claim is block-level G4-exactness; pair-level G4 for Controller-owned state (octant normalisation, the run ramp) is the Controller's.
475	
476	#### 11.3 The read view (TR-shipbody-029, -043)
477	
478	`read_view(ctx)` is called once at the registry freeze and puts a long-lived getter-only `BodyView` over the block (with `body_view_empty.gd` as the `empty_view` twin: neutral values, `is_empty()` true). All hot reads are typed scalars or fill a caller-owned buffer, so nothing allocates (`CNT-03` per accessor). `body.state` is `SIM`, never `PERCEPTION_OUT`; there is no per-player variant of any Body read; the Perception Filter draws its class-(c) rig at the true position and sanity never touches the block.
479	
480	| Read (names; scalars unless noted) | Readers |
481	|---|---|
482	| `pos_x(actor)`, `pos_y(actor)`; `prev_x(actor)`, `prev_y(actor)` | PRESENTATION; Emitter ACTOR anchor (`pos_curr` is already an integer: the anchor is `pos_curr` itself, no flooring step exists); Lighting shadow origin. **SIM readers of `prev_*` only from a hook ordered after `body.integrate`** |
483	| `body_of_actor(actor)`, `seat_of_actor(actor)`, `actor_of_seat(seat)`, `kind_of(actor)`, `actor_count()` | Controller, Emitter partition, Lighting masks, Interaction |
484	| `foot_box_into(actor, out)`, `foot_boxes_into(body, out) -> int` (ascending `actor_id`, **unfiltered, including unbound seats**) | Interaction `validate` (gathers boxes for Layout's `leaf_would_overlap`), Assembly |
485	| `actor_section(actor) -> section_id or 0`, `actor_local_x(actor)`, `actor_local_y(actor)` | Suit. **Derived on demand** as `section_at(body_of(actor), pos_curr)`; `actor_local_px = pos_curr - section_offset`; never stored, never cached across a mutator; the foot ORIGIN decides; NONE on a Layout body is a defect-only state counted `BDY_TRANSFER_NO_SECTION` (CI asserts zero in a clean build) |
486	| `actors_overlapping_into(body, rects: PackedInt32Array, out) -> int`; `actors_on_into(body, out) -> int` (ascending) | Assembly `validate` of a PLAYER cut, Transit |
487	| `world_x/_y(body)`, `vel_x/_y(body)`, `world_prev_x/_y(body)` | `body.projector`, Pipeline canvas offsets, Transit, `docked` (lint `BDY-04`) |
488	| `docked(a, b, shift_x, shift_y)`, `body_count()`, `odometer(actor)`, `trapped_into(out) -> int` | Assembly, Transit, Presenter (odometer frame index), Debug, Save/Load's autosave guard |
489	| `moved_x(actor)`, `moved_y(actor)` := `pos_curr - pos_prev`, derived on each call | **SIM-readable only by a hook registered `after: [body.integrate]`** (§ 12 lint `BDY-02`): then it is a difference of two tick-boundary values and G4-exact; before `body.integrate` it would read last tick's value in play and 0 on the first post-restore tick. The reader is `controller.noise` (TR-shipbody-042) |
490	| `blocked(actor)` | **PRESENTATION and DIAGNOSTIC only; never a SIM hook** (lint `BDY-03`): a SIM hook that read it would make it sim state that must be persisted and hashed (a schema bump, deliberately) |
491	
492	**Neighbour contracts (TR-shipbody-043), stated as Body's half.** Suit calls Layout `room_at(section_id, actor_local_px)` with **section-local** pixels (never body-frame `pos_curr`) and treats a NONE answer, or a plate-cell answer, as exterior exposure; a footprint-resident exempt actor (wall or hull-plate cap) is therefore EXPOSED, while a door-leaf exemption answers the door's `sill_room` and is not. Interaction reads `foot_boxes_into` unfiltered and ascending. Emitter and Lighting anchor on `pos_curr`. Those are the neighbours' own ADRs (0027, 0020, 0017, 0028); Body supplies the reads and fixes their order and domain. The GDD's `PERCEPTION` statement (PCI:216) is unchanged.
493	
494	#### 11.4 Trapped-actor probe (diagnostic only)
495	
496	At each detection event (placement, a transfer, `post_restore`, and a weld or cut for every actor on the touched bodies) and on each `trapped_into` read, Body runs for every actor whose start box gives a non-empty `E` a bounded read-only probe: for each of the four axis directions it repeats the admitted 1-px sub-step of § 5.4 up to `TILE_PX` times from the actor's pose, writing nothing, and asks whether the box reaches a pose that intersects no SOLID rectangle. If none of the four directions does the actor is TRAPPED: `BDY_TRAPPED_ACTOR` counts and `trapped_into` lists it. Cost: at most `4 * TILE_PX` overlap tests plus `section_at` calls per flagged actor, once per event and never inside `body.integrate`. The list is recomputed on every read, never cached, not persisted, not hashed, so a stale entry cannot suppress an autosave. The autosave guard is Save/Load's must-repeat (Body will never rescue).
497	
498	#### 11.5 Events and dirty keys
499	
500	Dirty keys use `DirtyKey.make(kind, id)` = `(kind << 32) | id` with `BODY 2` (key space of this block; reuse of Layout's number is legal because keys are namespaced by block) and `ACT 4`. **Every tick in which a persisted field changed marks a key** (`quiet_writes_allowed = false`): the hook marks `ACT/<actor_id>` for each actor whose position, `sub`, `last_octant` or `odometer` changed and `BODY/<body_id>` for each body whose `world` changed; mutators mark exactly the keys of the table in § 9 (`ACT/<id>` per moved actor, `BODY/<id>` per touched pose row). At most `MAX_ACTORS` plus `MAX_BODIES` keys per tick, far under `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS`; above it the kernel reports `ALL`. This is stricter than the ADR-0004 § 7 illustrative list that names Body among quiet blocks, and it is chosen so the debug missed-mark audit covers Body (§ Related asks that list to be amended). Keys are marked inside the mutator or hook, last, never from a setter (4.7 packed-array element writes call no setter).
501	
502	Events go through `scope.emit_event(&"body.state", kind, a0..a5)` and are P5 notifications that carry ids only:
503	
504	| Kind (id) | a0 | a1 | a2 | a3 | a4 | a5 |
505	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
506	| `BODY_TRANSFER` (1) | actor_id | old_body | new_body | frame_delta_x | frame_delta_y | cause (WELD 1, DETACH 2, POD 3) |
507	| `BODY_DOCK_CONTACT` (2) | surviving_body | absorbed_body | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
508	| `BODY_HULL_SEPARATION` (3) | old_body | new_body | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
509	
510	**Decision:** three event kinds, with `cause` an argument of `BODY_TRANSFER` (one kind per transfer would triple a subscriber's switch and the `PC_BODY_TRANSFER{detach|pod}` counter keys on cause). The GDD's seven-field `BODY_TRANSFER` record loses `tick` (the batch carries it) and `seat` (a subscriber reads `seat_of_actor(actor_id)` from the view; at the MVP an actor removed in the same batch is not a transfer), and `frame_delta_px` splits into two ints. `frame_delta` is the displacement the transfer applies to `pos_curr`, NEW minus OLD: `+shift` on a weld, `-shift` on a cut, `to_pos - pos_curr(old)` on a pod hop. The Pipeline rebases by it on a weld and a detach (the camera keeps its lag and the avatar's screen position does not move) and cuts on a pod hop or where the new body's bounds clamp; `body.projector` reparents the actor's Presenter node in the same tick (ADR-0034). Events raised in `INIT` and `RESTORE` scopes are discarded (ADR-0004 § 5).
511	
512	### 12. Determinism, tick indexing, lints and the fixtures that pin them
513	
514	**Determinism contract (G3, G4).** Order: bodies by ascending `body_id`, pose before actors, actors by ascending `actor_id`. Sweep input order is irrelevant (minimum over candidates) and asserted in debug. No float state, no wall clock, no RNG in the block or the hook (`SIM-02`, `SIM-03`). Tick-source independence: Body is correct for any number of `body.integrate` runs per rendered frame up to `MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME`; presenters see only the pair of the frame's last tick; four catch-up ticks at the maximum speed move at most 12 px, under the Pipeline's `JUMP_CUT`. Body does not choose the tick source (ADR-0001).
515	
516	**Tick-indexing convention (TR-horror-033, the Body half).** Seat commands issued in a rendered frame are admitted in P1 and applied in P2 of the next tick `t` that follows; `controller.step` (P3) writes `octant` and `gait_effective` from them; `body.integrate` in the **same tick** reads them and moves the actor; `horror.step` (ADR-0023) is ordered `after: body.integrate` and reads positions of tick `t` after they are written. Pinned by the fixture `TICKINDEX-1`: submit a `set_move_intent` east at frame `f`, run until the first tick that applies it, and assert in that tick (a) `controller.state.octant` is east after `controller.step`, (b) `pos_curr.x` advanced by `v_eff` after `body.integrate`, (c) a probe hook ordered `after: body.integrate` (standing in for `horror.step`) reads the advanced position, (d) a probe hook registered **without** the edge is rejected by the boot lint `STALE_EDGE_UNDECLARED` if it reads `moved`. The rule "a measured input-to-display latency above `INPUT_LATENCY_TICKS` on the RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK release exports forces `UNFOLD_LO` to 100" is **a data edit to the Horror tuning table, never code**; the S1 export run records the measured latency in its report so the edit has a number to act on (the threshold and `UNFOLD_LO` are Horror's; this ADR owns the convention and the measurement hook).
517	
518	**Lint pack `BDY-01` to `BDY-08`** (rule ids registered with ADR-0010's `modules.json` / `rules` config; tier E2 lexical unless noted):
519	- `BDY-01`: no script under `src/sim/body/` names `Node`, `Node2D`, `Camera2D`, `Viewport` (a specialisation of `SIM-01`), and `LocomotionStep` has no reference to `BodyState`. It also bans, in all of `src/sim/**`, the physics and navigation tokens `SIM-06` omits (§ 1).

530	### 13. Performance, counting gates and the `## @hot` list (TR-shipbody-034, -046)
531	
532	**Budget, stated once.** `body.integrate` is budgeted as **one hook** (pose step, every actor step including the exempt worst case, commit, dirty marking, diagnostics), not per actor: the cited figure is eight actors at 0.05 ms each, 0.4 ms, 20 % of the kernel's 2 ms P3 target; four actors at 0.2 ms is 10 %; a catch-up frame of `MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME` ticks is four hooks back to back (1.6 ms on the cited figure, 27 % of `FRAME_SIM_BUDGET_MS`). `STEP_BUDGET_MS` is only a logging threshold. **Every wall-clock figure is pending spike S1** on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK in a release export (Godot 4.7.2 `template_release`, `forward_plus`, vsync on, the Pipeline's 120-frame warm-up, with the renderer and driver read-back recorded): **P99 at most 90 % of the frame ceiling** (16.6 ms desktop, 33.3 ms deck), per-actor sweep logged above `SWEEP_COST_LOG_MS`. The developer machine is indicative only. The probe numbers of V4 (2.4 versus 23.8 microseconds per actor-tick at K = 16) are **not** a gate and are not evidence the hook fits; they show only that the analytic clamp is about an order of magnitude cheaper than the stepper on the editor binary, which is why it is the baseline.

595	### Implementation Guidelines
596	
597	- **Must** keep every `src/sim/body/` script `RefCounted`, scene-tree free and float-free; **must never** name a physics type, `Node`, a clock, an RNG or `randi`/`randf` (lint `SIM-01`, `SIM-02`, `SIM-03`, `SIM-06`).
598	- **Must** divide only through `IntMath` (`trunc_div` for the residue, `floor_div` for px-to-tile); **must never** write `/`, `%`, `min`, `max`, `abs`, `sign` or `clamp` in `src/sim/body/`.
599	- **Must** register `body.state` with `interpolated = true`, `gameplay = true`, `restore_after [layout.state]`, the hook with both `after` edges, the key space with `quiet_writes_allowed = false`, and fault domain 5; every kernel-invoked callable ends `return ctx.complete()`.
600	- **Must** write every mutator as `name(scope, ..., [out]) -> int` with `scope.open_for` first, the **whole** predicate before the first write, a defect that calls the sink, `scope.fault` and returns `-code`, and keys marked last; **must never** use `assert()`; **must never** call `scope.fault` on BM4's saturating branch.
601	- **Must** keep the persisted and derived columns in lock-step through the two private row functions; **must never** cache a row index, an `actor_section` answer or a `Dictionary` key across a mutator or a restore.
602	- **Must** copy columns into the snapshot payload (`Array` of ints, five keys); **must never** return a column, alias one, use `var_to_bytes` for a hashed byte or write a canonical byte writer.
603	- **Must** make exactly one `query_into` per moving actor per tick and none for a stationary one; **must never** ship the 1-px stepper in a non-test path.
604	- **Must** read only `octant` and `gait_effective` (and `has_row`) from the Controller; **must never** read `loco_state`, derive a gait or write any `controller.state` field.
605	- **Must** treat the rectangle set as read-only and as the only collision truth; **must never** inflate it, add a second set, push, shove, snap or eject an actor.
606	- **Must** keep `world_*` and `vel_*` out of every body-frame computation; **must never** let a SIM hook read `blocked`, or read `moved_*` / `prev_*` unless it is `after: [body.integrate]`.
607	- **Must** obtain every Body knob from `BodyTuning` and refuse a lowered bound without a `schema_version` bump (`BODY_BOUND_LOWERED`); **must never** hold a literal for a registered knob.
608	- **Must** cite `docs/registry` names for constants and **must never** retype a registry value.

610	## Alternatives Considered
611	
612	### Alternative 1: One `CharacterBody2D` per actor (or one `RigidBody2D` per ship) with engine collision shapes built from Layout
613	- **Description**: Build `CollisionShape2D`s from Layout's rectangles and move actors with `move_and_slide`.
614	- **Pros**: Free sliding, no custom sweep code, familiar to Godot users.
615	- **Cons**: Contradicts four designed GDDs; G3 and G4 would depend on a recorded physics replay (the server is not an integer system); a shape rebuild at every weld and every cut is unmeasured; engine collision needs margins and a safe-margin parameter that is a second rectangle set; rotation can leak inside the ship (Pipeline C2); the position would no longer be a pure function of the command stream.

616	- **Rejection Reason**: Determinism and the Pillar 1 rule that collision, light and drawing read one rectangle set. Not a close call.
617	
618	### Alternative 2: Engine-physics exterior hybrid (the ship's pose from a physics body, interiors on integers)
619	- **Description**: A `RigidBody2D` carries the hull while actors integrate in its frame.
620	- **Pros**: Real inertia and collision for hulks.
621	- **Cons**: A second authority for the pose; the pose would not be reproducible; Web Map & Transit already scripts constant-velocity legs; "a tumbling hulk" is an exterior sprite, never a simulation fact.
622	- **Rejection Reason**: Two authorities for one fact. Exterior motion is `world += vel` on integers.
623	
624	### Alternative 3: Ship the literal 1-px stepper
625	- **Description**: Test the destination box against every candidate for each of up to six sub-steps.
626	- **Pros**: Trivially correct, the specification itself, no equivalence proof needed.
627	- **Cons**: About `7 * K` rectangle tests per moving actor-tick against about `3 * K` for the clamp; the probe measured 23.8 versus 2.4 microseconds per actor-tick at K = 16 on the editor binary (indicative, not a gate), and in interpreted GDScript the tests dominate the hook.
628	- **Rejection Reason**: Cost. It is kept as the test oracle and as a debug cross-check mode, so correctness does not depend on trusting the clamp.
629	
630	### Alternative 4: Continuous swept-AABB with time of impact (float or fixed-point)
631	- **Description**: Compute a fractional hit time per rectangle and move to it.
632	- **Pros**: One computation regardless of step size.
633	- **Cons**: Needs division and fractional state, which the integer rules forbid; a rounding rule at the contact introduces a second residue; the result is not provably equal to the designed 1-px behaviour (a 1-px sliver, the first-legal-row corollary).
634	- **Rejection Reason**: The step is at most 3 px, so a per-axis integer clamp is exact and needs no fractions.
635	
636	### Alternative 5: Array of `RefCounted` actor records instead of struct-of-arrays
637	- **Description**: One object per actor with typed fields, kept in an `Array[ActorRow]`.
638	- **Pros**: Readable; each actor's fields travel together.
639	- **Cons**: One object dereference per field read in the hook; a per-row copy in the snapshot; the derived columns and the persisted ones would live on the same object, weakening the persisted/derived split that the reflection test enforces.
640	- **Rejection Reason**: SoA is the working assumption of the GDD and the cheaper hot loop; the snapshot shape is independent, so spike S1 can reverse it without a schema change (V6, OQ-1). Not a one-way door.
641	
642	### Alternative 6: Body derives sections by scanning, or caches `actor_section`
643	- **Description**: Keep a per-actor section id updated each tick.
644	- **Pros**: O(1) read for Suit.
645	- **Cons**: A stale value across a mutator (Suit reads after P2 of the next tick may have run a transfer); a second containment implementation to keep equivalent with Layout's.
646	- **Rejection Reason**: `section_at` is Layout's (ANSWERED in the GDD); Body derives on demand and never caches.
647	
648	### Alternative 7: Push out, eject or snap an actor that ends inside a footprint
649	- **Description**: Resolve a door-leaf closure or a cut by displacing the actor to the nearest free cell.
650	- **Pros**: Never leaves a trapped actor.
651	- **Cons**: An unannounced displacement the player did not cause (Pillar 2); contradicts PCI:650 "the body is never displaced" and LY-11; hides the authoring or Assembly defect that produced the overlap.
652	- **Rejection Reason**: Struck by the design. The guards are Assembly's refusal and deferral, BM4's apply-time refusal and the exempt-actor predicate.
653	
654	### Alternative 8: Position in the Controller block (PC-14 the other way)
655	- **Description**: `controller.state` owns the actor position and calls `LocomotionStep`.
656	- **Pros**: Fewer blocks.
657	- **Cons**: A pod hop or a detach changes the actor's body, which only Body tracks; the Layout projection inside an input system inverts the layering; replay would need the Controller's block to carry Layout knowledge.
658	- **Rejection Reason**: ADR-0019 § 1.2 ratifies PC-14; Body owns `pos`, `sub`, `odometer`.
659	
660	### Alternative 9: Roll `pos_prev` in `commit_baseline` at P4
661	- **Description**: Let the kernel's baseline roll maintain the pair, as a block with a plain current value would.
662	- **Pros**: Uses the kernel mechanism as written.
663	- **Cons**: At P5, when presenters read, `prev == curr`, which erases interpolation; it would also zero `moved` before any P5 reader and break the same-tick `controller.noise` contract.
664	- **Rejection Reason**: The roll is in the hook and the mutators; `commit_baseline` is a documented no-op. The cost is an ADR-0003 clarification (§ Related).
665	
666	### Alternative 10: Packed arrays in the snapshot payload
667	- **Description**: Emit `PackedInt32Array` / `PackedInt64Array` columns.
668	- **Pros**: Matches ADR-0011 and ADR-0013; fewer variants on the binary path.
669	- **Cons**: Contradicts TR-shipbody-008's "plain Arrays" and hides the type-walk failure class on the JSON path.
670	- **Rejection Reason**: The payload is a few hundred bytes; plain Arrays keep the TR text and the `BDY_RESTORE_TYPE` check meaningful. Reversible with a schema bump and a golden-file update.
671	
672	### Alternative 11: `Callable` for `collide` and for the mismatch sink
673	- **Description**: Bind `solid_in_into` and the sink as stored `Callable`s.
674	- **Pros**: No port class.
675	- **Cons**: `Callable.call(` is a `SIM-12` finding; `Callable(` / `.bind(` are `HOT-01` tokens; no typed signature; harder to double.
676	- **Rejection Reason**: `@abstract` ports are ADR-0010's pattern and cost one direct method call.
677	
678	### Alternative 12: Snap each body's canvas offset to the 24-px grid, or hide a docking jump behind the camera cut
679	- **Description**: Make a non-docked weld invisible to the exterior layer.
680	- **Pros**: Welds could be offered anywhere.
681	- **Cons**: Snapping moves a hull the player sees move; the camera cut hides camera motion, not the absorbed hull's jump (struck by the GDD's re-review).
682	- **Rejection Reason**: The offer gate (`docked`) is the only guard; it gates the offer, never Body's validate.
683	
684	## Consequences
685	
686	### Positive
687	- No physics server, body or area exists on any simulation path, so G3 and G4 do not depend on a recorded physics replay and a weld or cut rebuilds no engine shape.
688	- One implementation of the kinematics (`LocomotionStep.step_into`) serves Body now and Horror later; the value form and the hot form return identical results by construction.
689	- The analytic clamp is an order of magnitude cheaper than the literal stepper on the editor binary and is proven equal to it by a committed property test and, in the probe, on 300,000 random fixtures; the oracle remains in the repository as a debug cross-check.
690	- `body.state` is a plain, tiny, canonical block: five keys, a closed fault domain, an idempotent restore with a fixed answer for `REBASE_BLOCKS`, and a post-mutator invariant checked after every call, including faulted ones.

### Negative
- `interpolated = true` with a no-op `commit_baseline` departs from the plain reading of ADR-0003 and needs a one-line clarification there.
- SoA means two parallel column sets that must stay index-aligned; the two row functions and the alignment test are the cost.
- Plain-Array snapshots differ in style from ADR-0011 and ADR-0013 (deliberate, § 11.1).
- The exempt path is a literal per-sub-step predicate, not a closed form; it is bounded (six sub-steps) and defect-only, but it is code that the analytic clamp does not cover.
- BM1's return convention and the frame-shift argument shape change from the GDD, and the GDD, TR-shipbody-020 and four consumer GDDs must be synced.
- Body now depends on four things from siblings that do not yet exist (a body-liveness read, `section_contains`, `QueryBuffer`/`solid_in_into`, `ControllerView.has_row`).

## Risks
- **R1: GDScript cost of the whole hook is unmeasured (V5).** All wall-clock claims are UNVERIFIED. *Mitigation*: S1 on both reference machines before the hook story closes; the count gates catch algorithmic regressions meanwhile; the rung-3 GDExtension escape hatch (ADR-0010 § 9) is available only for the Graph at VS-A and is not assumed here.
- **R2: The clamp and the stepper diverge on an input the fixtures do not cover.** *Mitigation*: the committed grid (48 by 48 by 49 by 5), the random-fixture soak in CI with `BODY_SWEEP_CHECK`, and the oracle kept in-tree; any difference is a test failure.
- **R3: `solid_in_into`'s order or content differs from the assumed shape (ADR-0014 is a draft).** *Mitigation*: the sweep is order-independent; `LayoutCollide` is the single adapter; the unordered debug signal; a contract test against the real ADR-0014 implementation.
- **R4: Index misalignment between persisted and derived columns after a mutator.** *Mitigation*: only two row functions touch both; the alignment test after every mutator, restore and hook run.
- **R5: A mutator faults mid-apply and leaves Graph and Layout applied but Body not.** *Mitigation*: this is the documented no-rollback property of ADR-0003 § 5 (a fault is terminal until reload); Body's check-then-write guarantees only that Body itself is never half-applied; ADR-0021 may snapshot and restore the four touched blocks.
- **R6: Float32 canvas bound fails on a release export.** *Mitigation*: V3 is probed on the editor build; the repeat rides ADR-0008's spike; the fallback is a sign-split or a lowered limit with a schema bump (§ 2 ledger).
- **R7: A late consumer adds a SIM read of `blocked` or `world_*`.** *Mitigation*: lints `BDY-02` to `BDY-04`; the invariance fixture.
- **R8: A save made with a larger `MAX_ACTORS` is rejected by a build with a smaller one (`BDY_RESTORE_CAPACITY`)** against the principle that a build change must not make a save unloadable. *Mitigation*: the bounds ledger refuses a lowered bound without a schema bump; Open Question 13 of the GDD is answered by treating the cap as a save-compatibility fact.
- **R9: The `controller.noise` contract silently regresses if a hook drops its `after` edge.** *Mitigation*: `BDY-02` plus the registry-level CI test, and `TICKINDEX-1`.
- **R10: Stale reasoning about row indices.** *Mitigation*: no cached index, section id or Dictionary key across a mutator (a code-review checklist item and a test that mutates between reads).

## Performance Implications
- **CPU**: One hook per tick, divisor 1. Per moving actor one `query_into` and about `3 * K` rectangle tests (K is the rectangles in the swept cells, far below `MAX_FOOTPRINT_RECTS_PER_BODY`); a stationary actor costs the residue update, one copy and a possible dirty mark. The cited budget is 0.05 ms per actor, 0.4 ms for eight, against a 2 ms P3 target: **pending S1** (no wall-clock figure is a gate until recorded on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK in a release export). The editor-binary probe (2.4 microseconds per actor-tick at K = 16, both axes) is indicative only.
- **Memory**: Persisted columns for eight actors and a few bodies: about 4 KB at worst; derived columns the same order; one `QueryBuffer` sized once at boot to `MAX_FOOTPRINT_RECTS_PER_BODY`; the snapshot copy is a few hundred integers. No per-tick allocation (`HOT-01`, `CNT-01` to `CNT-03`).
- **Load Time**: `restore` is a cold pass over a few hundred integers plus one liveness check per distinct body; negligible next to Layout's rebuild.
- **Network**: None at the MVP (`SHARED_SUMMARY` replication is VS-B; no client-side prediction).

## Migration Plan
Greenfield: no code exists. Implementation order for the Body epic: (1) `IntMath` golden tests and `LocomotionTables`; (2) `LocomotionStep` with `SweepOracle` and the `SWEEP-EQ` grid; (3) `BodyState`/`BodyDerived`, the two row functions and the alignment test; (4) snapshot/restore/`default_state` with `BODY-RT` and `GOLDEN-1`; (5) BM1/BM2, then BM6/BM7, then BM3/BM4/BM5 against ADR-0013's records; (6) the hook, `TICKINDEX-1`, `INERTIAL-1`; (7) the read view, lints `BDY-01` to `BDY-08`; (8) spike S1 harness; (9) integration closure against the real kernel and Save/Load (AC-BDY-6 and AC-BDY-138 gate the epic). The GDD sync items (§ Related) land before stories are written from this ADR.

## Validation Criteria
- `SWEEP-EQ` passes with zero tolerance; the random-fixture soak with `BODY_SWEEP_CHECK` finds no difference; the analytic clamp is the only sweep in the release hook.
- `BODY-RT` (restore and re-snapshot at every tick of a 600-tick, three-phase run) is byte-identical; `GOLDEN-1` matches; `restore` rejects each named input with its named code and leaves the live block untouched.
- `MUT-CONS` holds I1 to I5 after every call of a generated sequence including faulted and saturating calls; a faulting call changes no byte of `snapshot()` and no dirty key.
- `INERTIAL-1` byte-identity; `TICKINDEX-1` ordering; the `moved` reader's registry-level `after` assertion.
- Count gates: at most one `query_into` per moving actor per tick, none for a stationary one, zero per-tick `origin_in_body` for a non-exempt actor; `CNT-01` unchanged over 600 ticks.
- S1: P99 of the whole hook at most 90 % of the frame ceiling on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK in a release export; nightly benchmark within +25 % of the baseline; SoA versus array-of-records recorded (V5, V6).
- Release-export repeat of V2 and V3 (LINT-SPIKE-1 and ADR-0008's spike) agree with the editor probes.
- `BDY_*` clean-build counters: `PC_FOOTPRINT_OVERLAP`, `BDY_TRAPPED_ACTOR`, `BDY_REBASE_ACTOR_IN_CAP`, `BDY_TRANSFER_NO_SECTION`, `BDY_PLAN_MISMATCH` read 0 in every clean scenario.

## Related

- **Registry stances relied on**: see Context. This ADR proposes the registry entries listed in the workflow output (`state_ownership` for `body.state`; interfaces for the mutators, `LocomotionStep`, the read view, the ports and the events; the analytic-clamp and in-hook-pair API decisions; forbidden patterns for engine physics on a simulation path, actor displacement, SIM reads of `blocked`/`world_*`, and cached row indices). No registry file is edited here.
- **Foundation ADRs and the asks this ADR makes of them** (not worked around): ADR-0003 (state that an owner may keep the interpolated pair in its own hook with a no-op `commit_baseline`, and that `snap_baseline`'s `key` is ignored for `SHARED` blocks; the published `can_*` naming divergence, already recorded by ADR-0013); ADR-0002 § 4 (the `binding_source` `ctx.put` payload shape; Body assumes `PackedInt64Array` pairs in ascending `seat`); ADR-0004 § 7 (the illustrative quiet-block list names Body; Body declares `quiet_writes_allowed = false`); ADR-0006 § 2.2 (list `body.state` outside `REBASE_BLOCKS`, closed list with no Body member); ADR-0010 (register lints `BDY-01` to `BDY-08`, the `## @hot` list of § 13, the `body_readers.json` and `body_bounds.lock.json` config files, `src/sim/body/ports/` as a port directory); ADR-0007 (the two `CONTENT_INVARIANT` names `BODY_FOOT_W_EVEN` and `BODY_BROADPHASE_CELL`, the `[0, 0]` range of `DETACH_DRIFT_PX_PER_TICK`).
- **Sibling assumptions (cross-ADR)**:
  - ADR-0014 (same wave, forward reference): `solid_in_into(body_id, ax0, ay0, ax1, ay1, out: QueryBuffer) -> int` returns the count of SOLID rectangles in their current leaf state intersecting the half-open box, body frame, unique, ascending `rect_key`, allocation-free; `QueryBuffer` exposes `x0, y0, x1, y1` (`PackedInt32Array`), `keys` (`PackedInt64Array`) and a count, sized once to `MAX_FOOTPRINT_RECTS_PER_BODY`; the result reflects the post-cut set from P2 and the post-`layout.doors` leaf set from P3 of the tick; callable by Horror as well as Body.
  - ADR-0013: a hot `body_is_live(body_id) -> bool` and a static `section_contains(section_id, local_x, local_y) -> bool` (own half-open cell set) are added to the Tier-H list of § 11 (not present in the draft); `section_at`, `section_offset_x/_y` and `body_of` as listed; `AttachResult` and `DetachResult` consumed verbatim (§ 9); Layout never reads `body.state`; the `can_*` naming divergence stays its ask.
  - ADR-0019: `ControllerView.octant(player_id)`, `gait_effective(player_id)` and a `has_row(player_id) -> bool` getter (the draft lists `row_count`); **Body does not read `intent_octant`** (strike it from the § 2.6 sentence "Body reads `octant`, `gait_effective` and `intent_octant`", TR-shipbody-016 binds two fields); Body publishes `body_of_actor`, `seat_of_actor`, `actor_of_seat` (the "pod-body test" ADR-0019 lists is Layout's or Transit's, not Body's); `controller.step` before `body.integrate`, `controller.noise` after it; the Controller clears only channel fields on a body edge and never writes Body.
  - ADR-0021: calls BM3 and BM4 after the Graph and Layout mutators in one scope, checks each status and stops on the first negative; repeats the `docked` offer gate and the cap-overlap refusal (V5); passes Layout's records unchanged.
  - ADR-0026: Web Map calls BM1, BM5, BM6, BM7 only inside the listed atomic applies, owns the `REORIGIN_IS_TRANSLATION` lint and the `WEB_COORD_BUDGET_PX` bound.
  - ADR-0034: `body.projector` subscribes to `body.state` (`BODY`/`ACT` keys, the three events), reparents on `BODY_TRANSFER`, computes `canvas_offset_render` from `world` and `world_prev`, owns the entity-id namespaces.
  - ADR-0023: Horror constructs `LocomotionStep`, supplies its own `CollideSource`, keeps its position in `horror.state`, and registers `horror.step` after `body.integrate`.
  - ADR-0016: `restore_after [layout.state]`, the seat-binding rebuild from `binding_source`, and verifiers; the Assembly invariant "INV-4 one Body pose row per live body" must read "at most one row per body, every row's body live" (a live body with no row is the legal sparse zero).
  - ADR-0027, ADR-0020, ADR-0017, ADR-0028: read contracts of § 11.3.
  - ADR-0033: the presentation-only debris exemption of `SIM-06` lives on a presentation path.
- **Design documents**: `design/gdd/ship-body-and-interior-physics.md` (owner), `design/gdd/ship-section-and-layout-data-model.md`, `design/gdd/player-controller-input.md`, `design/gdd/modular-ship-assembly.md`, `design/gdd/web-map-and-transit.md`, `design/gdd/horror-entities.md`, `design/gdd/pixel-perfect-render-pipeline-camera.md`, `design/gdd/command-simulation-layer.md`.

## Open Questions

If not, the fallbacks in order are: index-addressed `step_row` that bypasses the scratch copy (a second code path, so only with an equivalence test), an array-of-records or SoA re-layout (no schema change), then the GDExtension rung (ADR-0010 § 9, VS-A scope only).
