findings.text: § 11.2 phase 2 says columns are 'assigned from the scratch's own arrays' while 'the object is never replaced'. Assigning `state.a_x = scratch_a_x` replaces the packed array reference and makes the live column alias the scratch (probed: a write through `scratch` is visible in `state.a_x`, and a pre-existing alias keeps the old data). The facade survives because BodyState is the same object, but any cached column alias is stale, and a retained scratch aliases live state. `PackedInt32Array.assign()` does not exist on 4.7.2 (probed), so it cannot be the 'copy in place' fix.
findings.amendment: Say restore builds the scratch as fresh locals discarded after phase 2 (never a member), or does `resize` plus an element copy loop (cold path). Forbid caching a packed column in any member of `BodyView`, the hook, or `LayoutCollide` (loop-local aliases only, as § 7 already says), and add a test that restores and then reads through a pre-held view.

findings.text: The § 1 additions to the SIM-06/BDY-01 token list are incomplete for 2D physics. Missing entries that can answer collision or overlap questions on a sim path: `RayCast2D`, `ShapeCast2D`, `KinematicCollision2D`, `PhysicsRayQueryParameters2D`, `PhysicsPointQueryParameters2D`, `PhysicsDirectBodyState2D`, `CollisionObject2D`, `CollisionShape2D`, `CollisionPolygon2D`, `direct_space_state`, `get_world_2d`, and the TileMapLayer `collision_enabled` property. Most are Node subclasses, so SIM-01 may catch them only by exact name.
findings.amendment: Add those tokens to the BDY-01 list in § 1 and § 12, and to the ask to ADR-0010. Note that the engine's 2D physics server still exists and ticks with no bodies (harmless), so the guarantee is 'no use', not 'not instantiated'.

findings.text: § 11.1 uses plain bare `Array` payloads and `typeof` walks over a Variant tree. ADR-0010 SIM-09 bans bare `Array`/`Variant` in `src/sim`, and snapshot code needs an `dictionary_variant.json`-style allow-list entry that the ADR does not request. The justification 'the type walk still needed on the JSON path' is moot: ADR-0006 § 1.3 says the JSON dump is diagnostics only, never a load path (and `JSON.parse` yields floats for all numbers, so ints could not round-trip anyway). The typed-versus-untyped alternative is also not engine-blocked, since ADR-0005 encodes typed and untyped arrays identically.
findings.amendment: Add to the ADR-0010 asks: an allow-list entry for `body_state` snapshot/restore code (bare `Array`, `Variant`). Reword the Alternative 10 and § 11.1 rationale to the binary path only.

findings.text: Notes on the probed claims. V3 reproduced (8388609 and -8388609 round-trip; 16777217 becomes 16777216). Exact integer representability of `Node2D.position` is not sub-pixel precision: at 2^22 the float32 ulp is 0.5 px and at 2^23 it is 1 px. The `floor()` in `canvas_offset_render` is therefore load-bearing, not cosmetic, and an unfloored interpolation at large offsets would quantise. `>>` on a negative literal is a parse error ("Only positive operands are supported"), while a negative variable shifts arithmetically at runtime (-5 >> 1 = -3, probed), so the ADR's only use (`FOOT_BOX_W >> 1`, positive and boot-checked even) is safe. `Array`/`posmod`/`mini`/`maxi`/`absi`/`signi`/`clampi` exist with int returns.
findings.amendment: In § 10, state that `canvas_offset_render` must floor before assigning to `Node2D.position` and that `>>` must never receive a negative operand in `src/sim/body/`. Keep the release-export repeat of V2/V3 as already planned.

cross_adr.text: ADR-0015 § 5.1 and § Related assume `solid_in_into(body_id, ax0, ay0, ax1, ay1, out) -> int` with `QueryBuffer` columns `x0, y0, x1, y1` (half-open, body frame) as PackedInt32Array, wrapped by `CollideSource.bind(body_id)` plus `query_into`. ADR-0014 instead publishes `SolidQuery.solid_in(body_id, ax0, ay0, ax1, ay1, out)` with explicit `body_id` and no bind. Its QueryBuffer has one `spans` PackedInt32Array holding 4 values per record as an INCLUSIVE occupied span `(x0, y0, x1-1, y1-1)`, plus `status`, `flags`, `grew` and a `grow()` that can reallocate. ADR-0015's clamp (`r.x0 >= bx1`, `limit = r.x0 - bx1`) is derived for half-open rectangles. A naive `LayoutCollide` that reads `spans` as half-open is off by one on every wall contact and would be caught only by SWEEP-EQ. ADR-0014 line 34 also says Body's LocomotionStep 'takes a SolidQuery', but ADR-0015 defines `CollideSource`.
cross_adr.amendment: Reconcile in ADR-0014/0015 before either is Accepted. ADR-0015 should name `SolidQuery` as the Layout-side port, keep `CollideSource` as the Body-side seam, and state that `LayoutCollide` converts inclusive spans to half-open (+1 on x1, y1) in exactly one place (or ADR-0014 exposes a half-open view). Drop `bind` (see E1). Both ADRs should state that `QueryBuffer.grow()` is cold and must not run inside `step_into` (size the buffer to `MAX_FOOTPRINT_RECTS_PER_BODY` at boot, or treat `status` or `grew` as a counted defect).

cross_adr.text: V8 is answerable now. `Node.reparent(new_parent, keep_global_transform = true)` defaults to preserving the global transform (probed on 4.7.2): reparenting a Node2D at local (10, 20) from a parent at x=1000 to a parent at x=-500 rewrites its local position to (1510, 20) and keeps global (1010, 20); `reparent(p, false)` keeps local and moves global by the offset difference. On a `BODY_TRANSFER` the projector must therefore set the presenter's local position from the new `pos_curr` after reparenting, not rely on either default. Canvas-offset differences up to ±2^23 are exact in float32, so no precision is lost.
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0034 should state which `keep_global_transform` it uses on BODY_TRANSFER and that it writes the local position explicitly from `BodyView.pos_x/pos_y` in the same tick. ADR-0015 V8 can be marked 'answered by probe 2026-10-29 (review), pending ADR-0034 scene shape'.

cross_adr.text: Four lint-config asks arise from this review. (1) HOT-01's `.bind(` token collides with any port method named `bind` (E1). (2) SIM-06 and the BDY-01 additions omit RayCast2D, ShapeCast2D and the other 2D collision classes (E8). (3) SIM-09 needs a documented allow-list entry for Body snapshot/restore Variant/Array code (E9). (4) With UNUSED_PARAMETER and SHADOWED_VARIABLE at 2, the port, kernel-callable and double signatures in § 3 and § 9 need the underscore-prefix convention (E6).
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0010 should add the tokens in E8 to SIM-06, add the `body_state` allow-list entry, and document in § 3.5 that port methods must not be named `bind`, and that unused parameters in kernel-signature callables and port doubles are `_`-prefixed.

findings.text: `collide.bind(body_id)` is called inside `BodyModule._hook_integrate`, which the ADR tags `## @hot`. ADR-0010 HOT-01 bans the token `.bind(` (as `Callable.bind`), and § 5.1 and § 7 repeat that ban. The lexical scan cannot tell a port method from `Callable.bind`, so the ADR's own hook fails BDY-06/HOT-01 as written. No Object or RefCounted method named `bind` exists (probed), so it is a lint clash, not an engine clash. It is also redundant: ADR-0014's `solid_in` takes `body_id` per call.
findings.amendment: Rename the port method to `bind_body(body_id)` or drop it and pass `body_id` to `query_into` and `origin_in_body` (matches ADR-0014). Update § 5.1, § 7, the Key Interfaces block, and the `CountingCollide` wording. Do not carve a HOT-01 exemption.

findings.text: § 2 says `LocomotionTables` holds `UNIT_X[8]`, `UNIT_Y[8]` and `ODO_W[8]` as constants, but gives no declaration form. The obvious form `const UNIT_X := PackedInt32Array([256, 181, ...])` does not compile on 4.7.2: probed, "Assigned value for constant isn't a constant expression". `const A = PackedInt32Array()` fails the same way. These forms work: `const A: PackedInt32Array = [256, 181, ...]` (probed: typeof is TYPE_PACKED_INT32_ARRAY), `const A: Array[int] = [...]`, and `static var` with a constructor. `Vector2i(...)` consts also work. The ADR's other consts (int expressions such as `(DOMAIN_ID << 16) | 1`, and `const NAMES: Array[StringName] = [&"", &"X"]`) compile (probed).
findings.amendment: In § 2 and the Key Interfaces block, state the form: `const UNIT_X: PackedInt32Array = [..]` (or `Array[int]`), never `PackedInt32Array([..])` in a `const`. Add a one-line load test for `LocomotionTables` to the golden test. Note that a const array is read-only, so the hot path only reads it.

findings.text: Writing an int into a PackedInt32Array element wraps silently with no error or warning. Probed: `a[0] = 1<<31` gives -2147483648 and `a[1] = (1<<32)+5` gives 5. NARROWING_CONVERSION does not fire for int to int. § 11.2 step 4 range-checks `sub`, `octant`, `odometer`, `heading` and the pose, but not `pos_x`/`pos_y`, `body_id`, or `seat` (only `>= 0`). § 4.1 stores these in int32 columns, and `kind` is only checked against two values. A decoded payload with a value at or above 2^31 would pass Phase 1, wrap in Phase 2, and break the claims 'first failure wins' and `snapshot(restore(x)) == x`. The same hole exists in the mutator arguments `x`, `y`, `shift_*`, `seat` and `to_body_id`.
findings.amendment: Add a Phase 1 rule: every value destined for an int32 column must lie inside explicit bounds (`body_id` 1..2^31-1, `seat` 0..MAX_SEAT, `pos_*` within a stated body-frame limit, shifts within it), failing with a new local code `BDY_RESTORE_COLUMN_RANGE` (append-only, domain 5 local 33) or an existing one. Mirror the bounds in `can_place`, `can_transfer` and `can_rebase_*`, so apply-time never writes an out-of-range int32. Add a MUT-CONS/BODY-RT fixture with 2^31 and 2^32+5.

findings.text: § 4 says 'row = bsearch position' but never says how absence is detected. `PackedInt64Array.bsearch(v)` always returns an insertion index (probed: `bsearch(2)` on [1,3,2^53+7] returns 1; `bsearch(3, false)` on a present value returns 2 and the default `before=true` returns 1). A row for an absent id can therefore be `size()`, and an unchecked `a_id[row]` read is out of range. In a release export that read logs an error and yields 0. That is exactly the 'stale row' failure R10 worries about, and it is not caught by 'no cached index'. The § 11.3 getters (`pos_x(actor)` etc.) and BM2/BM5 on an unknown actor are the exposed paths.
findings.amendment: Specify a single private `_find_actor_row(id) -> int` returning -1 unless `row < a_id.size() and a_id[row] == id` (same for bodies), with `before=true`. All getters return a neutral value on -1 and mutators return `BDY_UNKNOWN_ACTOR`. Add a unit test for absent ids at the first, middle, last and past-the-end positions.

findings.text: The § 7 pseudocode `blocked[i] := result.blocked` (a `bool` into `BodyDerived.a_blocked: PackedByteArray`) is invalid GDScript. Probed on 4.7.2: "Invalid assignment of property or key '0' with value of type 'bool' on a base object of type 'PackedByteArray'". It would fail at load or error every tick inside the hook.
findings.amendment: State `a_blocked[i] = 1 if r.blocked else 0` in § 7, and read it as `a_blocked[i] != 0` in `BodyView.blocked`. This is allocation-free and HOT-01 clean.

findings.text: ADR-0010 sets SHADOWED_VARIABLE, SHADOWED_VARIABLE_BASE_CLASS, SHADOWED_GLOBAL_IDENTIFIER and UNUSED_PARAMETER to 2 (error). Probed with those at 2: a parameter named like an existing member fails ("local function parameter 'collide' is shadowing an already-declared variable"), and an unused parameter fails ("never used ... prefix it with an underscore"). `BodyModule.setup(facet, tuning, collide, layout, sink)` injects ports that the module stores in members. The natural member names `collide`, `layout`, `sink`, `tuning` would shadow the parameters. `snap_baseline(key, ctx)` deliberately ignores `key`, and `_hook_integrate(views, scope, ctx)` is similar. Test doubles of the ports ignore arguments.
findings.amendment: Add to Implementation Guidelines: stored ports are private members (`_collide`, `_layout`, `_sink`, `_tuning`); every intentionally unused kernel-signature or double parameter is underscore-prefixed (`_key`). Show `snap_baseline(_key: int, ctx: ...)` in § 8.

The justification 'the type walk still needed on the JSON path' is moot: ADR-0006 § 1.3 says the JSON dump is diagnostics only, never a load path (and `JSON.parse` yields floats for all numbers, so ints could not round-trip anyway). The typed-versus-untyped alternative is also not engine-blocked, since ADR-0005 encodes typed and untyped arrays identically.
findings.amendment: Add to the ADR-0010 asks: an allow-list entry for `body_state` snapshot/restore code (bare `Array`, `Variant`). Reword the Alternative 10 and § 11.1 rationale to the binary path only.

findings.text: Notes on the probed claims. V3 reproduced (8388609 and -8388609 round-trip; 16777217 becomes 16777216). Exact integer representability of `Node2D.position` is not sub-pixel precision: at 2^22 the float32 ulp is 0.5 px and at 2^23 it is 1 px. The `floor()` in `canvas_offset_render` is therefore load-bearing, not cosmetic, and an unfloored interpolation at large offsets would quantise. `>>` on a negative literal is a parse error ("Only positive operands are supported"), while a negative variable shifts arithmetically at runtime (-5 >> 1 = -3, probed), so the ADR's only use (`FOOT_BOX_W >> 1`, positive and boot-checked even) is safe. `Array`/`posmod`/`mini`/`maxi`/`absi`/`signi`/`clampi` exist with int returns.
findings.amendment: In § 10, state that `canvas_offset_render` must floor before assigning to `Node2D.position` and that `>>` must never receive a negative operand in `src/sim/body/`. Keep the release-export repeat of V2/V3 as already planned.

cross_adr.text: ADR-0015 § 5.1 and § Related assume `solid_in_into(body_id, ax0, ay0, ax1, ay1, out) -> int` with `QueryBuffer` columns `x0, y0, x1, y1` (half-open, body frame) as PackedInt32Array, wrapped by `CollideSource.bind(body_id)` plus `query_into`. ADR-0014 instead publishes `SolidQuery.solid_in(body_id, ax0, ay0, ax1, ay1, out)` with explicit `body_id` and no bind. Its QueryBuffer has one `spans` PackedInt32Array holding 4 values per record as an INCLUSIVE occupied span `(x0, y0, x1-1, y1-1)`, plus `status`, `flags`, `grew` and a `grow()` that can reallocate. ADR-0015's clamp (`r.x0 >= bx1`, `limit = r.x0 - bx1`) is derived for half-open rectangles. A naive `LayoutCollide` that reads `spans` as half-open is off by one on every wall contact and would be caught only by SWEEP-EQ. ADR-0014 line 34 also says Body's LocomotionStep 'takes a SolidQuery', but ADR-0015 defines `CollideSource`.
cross_adr.amendment: Reconcile in ADR-0014/0015 before either is Accepted. ADR-0015 should name `SolidQuery` as the Layout-side port, keep `CollideSource` as the Body-side seam, and state that `LayoutCollide` converts inclusive spans to half-open (+1 on x1, y1) in exactly one place (or ADR-0014 exposes a half-open view). Drop `bind` (see E1). Both ADRs should state that `QueryBuffer.grow()` is cold and must not run inside `step_into` (size the buffer to `MAX_FOOTPRINT_RECTS_PER_BODY` at boot, or treat `status` or `grew` as a counted defect).

cross_adr.text: V8 is answerable now. `Node.reparent(new_parent, keep_global_transform = true)` defaults to preserving the global transform (probed on 4.7.2): reparenting a Node2D at local (10, 20) from a parent at x=1000 to a parent at x=-500 rewrites its local position to (1510, 20) and keeps global (1010, 20); `reparent(p, false)` keeps local and moves global by the offset difference. On a `BODY_TRANSFER` the projector must therefore set the presenter's local position from the new `pos_curr` after reparenting, not rely on either default. Canvas-offset differences up to ±2^23 are exact in float32, so no precision is lost.
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0034 should state which `keep_global_transform` it uses on BODY_TRANSFER and that it writes the local position explicitly from `BodyView.pos_x/pos_y` in the same tick. ADR-0015 V8 can be marked 'answered by probe 2026-10-29 (review), pending ADR-0034 scene shape'.

cross_adr.text: Four lint-config asks arise from this review. (1) HOT-01's `.bind(` token collides with any port method named `bind` (E1). (2) SIM-06 and the BDY-01 additions omit RayCast2D, ShapeCast2D and the other 2D collision classes (E8). (3) SIM-09 needs a documented allow-list entry for Body snapshot/restore Variant/Array code (E9). (4) With UNUSED_PARAMETER and SHADOWED_VARIABLE at 2, the port, kernel-callable and double signatures in § 3 and § 9 need the underscore-prefix convention (E6).
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0010 should add the tokens in E8 to SIM-06, add the `body_state` allow-list entry, and document in § 3.5 that port methods must not be named `bind`, and that unused parameters in kernel-signature callables and port doubles are `_`-prefixed.
